title: Stop hoping reviewers catch bugs
summary: Stop hoping reviewers catch bugs: a Claude Code plugin checks every commit before the PR goes to GitHub.
body: Stop hoping reviewers catch bugs: a Claude Code plugin checks every commit before the PR goes to GitHub.

Our PRs kept landing with errors in them. The fix was one Claude plugin: a backpack of tools and rules Claude loads every session. Now every commit triggers it, it verifies and checks that everything works, and only then does the PR go up.
Plugins are guardrails. The code is correct before anyone else has to review it.

I'm Manraj Sidhu, AI developer, and this is the real setup my team uses.
Built with @claudeai @github

Which plugin would you build? Comment PLUGIN with your idea.
Follow @manrajtalks
guide: A Claude Code plugin that checks every commit before the pull request goes up. You need Claude Code, a GitHub repository and a few minutes to write your checks.
1. Decide what "correct" means for your project: the tests, the linter, the type check and any rules your team keeps repeating in reviews.
1. Write those checks as a Claude Code plugin, a bundle of instructions, commands and tools that Claude loads at the start of every session.
1. Add a Claude Code hook that fires the plugin whenever Claude makes a commit.
1. Have the plugin run your checks, read the output and fix what fails, then re-run until everything passes.
1. Stop the pull request being opened until the checks pass, using the hook or a rule in the plugin.
1. Open the pull request on GitHub with the GitHub CLI once the commit is clean.
1. Share the plugin with your team so everyone gets the same checks.
Watch out: the plugin only helps if it blocks the pull request when a check fails, so test it against a deliberately broken commit first.
